newsitem.title: USA: InterDigital gets favorable court ruling.
newsitem.headline: InterDigital gets favorable court ruling.

text.p: KING OF PRUSSIA, Pa., July 31 - InterDigital Communications Corp said Thursday that a federal appelate court reinstated two of its claims against Motorola Inc in a patent infringement suit.

The company said the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit partially rejected Motorola's appeal by affirming the validity of three InterDigital claims a lower court had found valid; granting two additional claims from wireless communications patents; and by refusing to grant attorneys fees to Motorola.

An InterDigital spokeswoman said the ruling does not give the company the right to sue Motorola for infringing on the five claims because the appelate court did not grant the company's request for a new trial.
"The court did affirm the validity of the claims, so we could pursue infringement by other companies," the spokeswoman said.
A U.S. District Court for the District of Delaware judge last year found three InterDigital patents valid (out of a total 24 claims) but not infringed upon by Motorola.
Motorola spokesmen were not immediately available to elaborate on the ruling.
InterDigital's stock traded at 5-11/16 Thursday morning, up 3/16.
